processing: A premium green tea finished into tight, straight strips. Picking and processing details are not published beyond the safety rules of its geographical indication.
harvest_season: No picking calendar is published; as with other premium Chongqing greens, it is usually a spring tea with the earliest pickings most valued.
appearance_dry: Tight, straight strips with a moist green sheen.
taste_profile: A lasting chestnut aroma over a full, mellow and refreshing body.

brewing.notes: General guidance for a tender straight-strip green rather than a local rule: water around 80 °C keeps the chestnut note clean and avoids bitterness.

vintage_note: Like other premium Chinese greens it is normally sold as the current year's harvest and is at its best within about a year. The name is tied closely to the Jinfo Yucui brand, so check the geographical indication mark and the harvest date on the pack.
description:
Jinfo Yucui is the premium green tea of Nanchuan in southern Chongqing, named after nearby Jinfo Mountain. Unlike many place-name teas it began as a brand: the protected name mainly refers to tea sold under the Jinfo Yucui label.

The registered area is wide, 29 townships and subdistricts at 600 to 1200 metres, split between a northern main growing zone and a central belt of fine greens. The mountain's old-tree tea, Nanchuan Dashu, is protected separately, and the two are easy to confuse.

Expect tight straight strips, a tender green cup and a lasting chestnut aroma, with a full but refreshing body. Chestnut is typical of roasted Chinese greens, so treat it gently with water around 80 °C and short first steeps.

This is positioned as a high-end tea and it has won a long list of competition awards, so the packaging will often lean on those. The harvest date and the mark tell you more than the medals.
history:
Tea growing in Nanchuan is claimed by local promoters to go back more than 1700 years, a figure given without a primary record. The Jinfo Yucui name itself is recent: its record of more than 20 international, national and regional awards spans roughly the last couple of decades.

It has been repeatedly listed among Chongqing's ten famous teas and is registered as an agricultural geographical indication, with about 4315 hectares of tea gardens and an output of 800 tonnes reported for the area. Who created the tea and exactly when is little documented.
